neighbours.label: the point in nutrition text where the food sources or the daily dose of a named vitamin or mineral are being listed (get vitamin E by eating ..., sources: nuts, fortified cereals ...); food lists with no nutrient framing stay quiet
fire: Folate is found in leafy greens, beans, oranges and fortified breads.
You can boost your vitamin A intake by eating carrots, sweet potatoes and kale.
Rich dietary sources of zinc: oysters, beef, pumpkin seeds and chickpeas.
To get enough calcium, eat yogurt, cheese, sardines and fortified orange juice.
Potassium is plentiful in bananas, potatoes, beans and dried apricots.
Vitamin K comes mainly from spinach, broccoli, cabbage and vegetable oils.
Good sources of selenium include Brazil nuts, tuna, eggs and whole grains.
Vitamin B12 is supplied by eating fish, meat, eggs and fortified cereals.
quiet: The picnic basket held sandwiches, grapes, lemonade and a bag of crisps.
You can brighten the hallway by hanging mirrors, lamps and framed prints.
Things to pack for camp: a sleeping bag, a torch, boots and sunscreen.
To make the stew, chop onions, carrots, celery and a few potatoes.
The market stall was piled with bananas, melons, peaches and dried figs.
Vitamin K was discovered in 1929 by a Danish biochemist studying chickens.
The orchestra includes violins, cellos, flutes and a pair of harps.
My grandfather spends his weekends eating out, fishing and fixing clocks.
